title: Hiking 02 - one dispute, one changed mind, one quiet member

messages.text: Ok team, November hiking trip. Let's pick a place this week.
I vote Patagonia. Torres del Paine, the W trek, done.
Dolomites for me. Rifugio to rifugio, pasta every night.
Banff. Cheap flights and I know the area.
Yosemite! Nobody needs a passport and we could drive.
I'm easy. Only constraint is I have to be home by the 22nd.
Noted. Dates Nov 14 to 21 then? Seven days.
Works for me.
Yes, works.
Works.
Works for me.
Nov 14-21 is good.
Budget? I was thinking $2,500 a head all in.
Fine.
Fine with me.
Same.
Yep.
Great. What matters most to each of you?
Hiking quality. I want proper mountains and big views.
Same, plus food. I'm a foodie, sorry.
Cost, and not being cold and wet.
Cost and low-stress logistics.
Random, but did anyone listen to that podcast about the Camino? Made me want to walk for a month.
Ha, one week first, Maya.
lol
I'd do the Camino after Patagonia.
Patagonia flights are about $1,300 round trip, I checked yesterday.
Dolomites flights are around $900. Trains from Venice are cheap too.
Just so you know, most Dolomites huts are closed in November.
Some rifugi stay open into early November though. I'm not sure about the 14th to the 21st.
I read that almost everything shuts by late October.
I've read the opposite for a few of the big ones. I'll check.
Jordan, Banff in mid-November, isn't that all snow?
Probably. I looked at trail conditions last year and half the trails were closed by then.
Ok, I'm dropping Banff. If it's not Banff I'd take the Dolomites over Patagonia because of cost.
Yosemite in November is also unpredictable. Tioga Pass usually closes.
Do we still want Yosemite, Maya?
Not really. Let's drop it. I'm fine with either Patagonia or the Dolomites.
I lean Patagonia, it's a bucket list thing for me too.
Obviously Patagonia.
I'm Dolomites, unless the huts turn out to be closed.
So it's 2 and 2 with Maya neutral. Leo?
Leo, any preference?
He's probably busy. Let's not wait on him.
Cost check. Patagonia is $1,300 in flights plus park fees. Is $2,500 realistic?
Yes, I did the math last week. Flights, the W trek refugios, food, all under $2,500.
Ok. Still, the Dolomites would leave more room.
Fair. It's a tradeoff between the bucket-list factor and cost.
Also, the Dolomites have decent public transport. Patagonia needs buses and ferries.
The buses run daily in season. November is early season but they run.
Season starts around October, I think? I'm not sure.
Yeah, October to April, I think.
Can we decide the tiebreak method? A vote?
Let's settle the hut question first. If the Dolomites huts are closed it's Patagonia by default.
Agreed, that's the fair way. I'll check the refugio opening dates.
And I'll check what's open in Torres del Paine in November so it's apples to apples.
Good plan.
Works for me.
Ok. Let's regroup Wednesday evening after Priya and Alex report back.
Sounds good.
Also, can someone make a shared doc for all of this?
I'll do it. A sheet with options, flights and notes.
Thanks Maya.
Thanks. I'll post what I find here Wednesday morning.
Same.
Great. Talk Wednesday.
